source_evidence.observation: Model 1 defines the input format by precision t, exponent range [e_min,e_max], u=2^(-t), f_min, f_max, and underflow bound g_min; it defines a nested accumulation format with T>=t, U=2^(-T), F_min, F_max, and G_min. Equation (2.3) models input rounding, assuming no overflow, as fl(x)=x(1+delta)+eta with |delta|<=u, |eta|<=g_min, and eta*delta=0.

Equation (2.4) applies the analogous model to each accumulation-format operation x op y, with op in {+,-,multiplication,division}, relative error bounded by U, underflow error bounded by G_min, and mutually exclusive errors. The default is round-to-nearest; directed rounding is covered by replacing u,g_min,U,G_min by 2u,2g_min,2U,2G_min.

The matrix product is diagonally scaled as Lambda^(-1) fl(Lambda A) fl(BM) M^(-1). Lambda and M are nonsingular diagonal power-of-two scalings. The paper assumes no underflow or overflow before the input scaling or after the inverse output scaling, with A, B, and C stored exactly in a sufficiently high-precision format.

The scaling threshold is theta=min(f_max,sqrt(F_max/n)). The construction chooses a maximal power-of-two row factor lambda and column factor mu satisfying theta/(2||x||_infinity)<lambda<=theta/||x||_infinity and theta/(2||y||_infinity)<mu<=theta/||y||_infinity.

In the single-word analysis, each accumulation underflow contributes at most 4 theta^(-2) G_min ||x||_infinity ||y||_infinity after inverse scaling, and the number r of such underflows in one length-n inner product is bounded by n.

Equation (3.26) is explicitly introduced as the result of dropping second-order terms from the exact bound (3.25), and uses the symbol lesssim. Its input-underflow coefficient is printed as 4n^2 theta^(-1) g_min, while its accumulation-underflow coefficient is 4n^2 theta^(-2) G_min.

A p-word representation uses p low-precision words indexed from 0 to p-1. The product retains the p(p+1)/2 pairs satisfying i+j<p. Equation (4.3) introduces the scaled recurrence w^(i)=fl((w-sum_{j=0}^{i-1}u^j w^(j))/u^i), designed to avoid rapid underflow of later words.

The scaled recurrence reconstructs w as sum_{i=0}^{p-1}u^i w^(i) with an order-u^p residual. Applied elementwise to Lambda A and BM, the induction through (4.13) bounds each final residual by the maximum of a rounding contribution u^p times the exact scaled entry and an underflow contribution u^(p-1)g_min.

Equations (4.18)-(4.20) give matrix decomposition residuals bounded by zeta=max(u^p,2n u^(p-1) theta^(-1)g_min). Equations (4.21)-(4.25) give the exact total-error decomposition, including decomposition errors, aggregate accumulation error Delta C, and omitted products. Equation (4.26) bounds the omitted products by lesssim (p-1)u^p ||A||_infinity||B||_infinity.

Equation (4.27) combines an imported order-(n+p^2)U accumulation-rounding estimate with accumulation underflows and r<=np(p+1)/2. Equation (4.28) combines all errors. Theorem 4.1 specifies the scaled input-format recurrences, retains i+j<p, computes every word-product inner product in the accumulation format, and states (4.32). Equation (4.33) is the cited range-unrestricted comparison.

The paper identifies the two terms shared with the range-unrestricted analysis as order u^p and U, and the two new underflow terms as order u^(p-1)theta^(-1)g_min and theta^(-2)G_min. It then says that the single-word input terms 2u and 4n theta^(-1)g_min are both reduced by a factor of order u^(p-1), despite equation (3.26) printing 4n^2 theta^(-1)g_min.

binders: Explicitly, A is an m-by-n real matrix and B is an n-by-q real matrix; consequently AB is m-by-q. [PDF p. 11 (B795), Theorem 4.1]

The theorem ranges over a p-word decomposition; section 4 defines p as the number of words and indexes words by 0,...,p-1, so p is inherited as a positive integer. [PDF p. 8 (B792), section 4 and equations (4.1)-(4.3)]
Lambda and M are diagonal power-of-two scaling matrices, necessarily of sizes m-by-m and q-by-q from the products Lambda A and BM. [PDF p. 11 (B795), Theorem 4.1]
For 0<=i,j<p, A^(i) has the shape of A and B^(j) has the shape of B. [PDF p. 11 (B795), equations (4.29)-(4.31)]
The parameters u,U,f_max,F_max,g_min,G_min are fixed by the selected input and accumulation formats in Model 1. [PDF p. 2 (B786), Model 1 and equations (2.1)-(2.3)]

C=AB denotes the exact real product, while C_hat denotes the result after the retained word products are evaluated in the accumulation format. [PDF p. 10 (B794), equations (4.21)-(4.25); PDF p. 11 (B795), equations (4.31)-(4.32)]
hypotheses: The computation uses a mixed-precision MMA unit satisfying Model 1, with an input format of unit roundoff u and an accumulation format of unit roundoff U. [PDF p. 11 (B795), Theorem 4.1; PDF p. 2 (B786), Model 1]

Explicitly in Theorem 4.1, every entry of Lambda A and BM is bounded in magnitude by theta=min(f_max,sqrt(F_max/n)), and the diagonal coefficients of Lambda and M are powers of two. [PDF p. 11 (B795), Theorem 4.1]

The intended preceding scaling construction chooses maximal power-of-two factors satisfying theta/(2||x||_infinity)<lambda<=theta/||x||_infinity for every row x and the analogous inequalities for every column y. [PDF p. 5 (B789), equations (3.4a)-(3.4b)]

The input words are formed elementwise by A^(i)=fl((Lambda A-sum_{k=0}^{i-1}u^k A^(k))/u^i) and B^(j)=fl((BM-sum_{k=0}^{j-1}u^k B^(k))/u^j), where fl rounds to the input format. [PDF p. 11 (B795), equations (4.29)-(4.30)]
Only word-product pairs satisfying i+j

The floating-point models assume that overflow does not occur; the selected theta is designed to prevent overflow in both input conversion and accumulation because theta<=f_max and n theta^2<=F_max. [PDF p. 2 (B786), equation (2.3); PDF p. 5 (B789), equation (3.2) and preceding paragraph]

The stated constants use round-to-nearest. Under directed rounding the paper requires the substitutions u->2u, g_min->2g_min, U->2U, and G_min->2G_min. [PDF p. 3 (B787), paragraph following equation (2.4)]

The surrounding analysis assumes A, B, and C are represented exactly in a sufficiently high-precision format before Lambda,M scaling and after Lambda^(-1),M^(-1) scaling, with no underflow or overflow in those outer stages. [PDF p. 4 (B788), equation (3.1) and following scaling-assumption paragraph; PDF p. 5 (B789), continuation of that paragraph]
conclusions: The proved decomposition identities are A=sum_{i=0}^{p-1}u^i Lambda^(-1)A^(i)+Delta A and B=sum_{j=0}^{p-1}u^j B^(j)M^(-1)+Delta B, with ||Delta A||_infinity<=zeta||A||_infinity, ||Delta B||_infinity<=zeta||B||_infinity, and zeta=max(u^p,2n u^(p-1)theta^(-1)g_min). [PDF p. 10 (B794), equations (4.18)-(4.20)]

Writing Delta C for aggregate accumulation-format error, equations (4.21)-(4.25) give C_hat=(A-Delta A)(B-Delta B)+Lambda^(-1)Delta C M^(-1)-sum_{i+j>=p}u^(i+j)Lambda^(-1)A^(i)B^(j)M^(-1)=AB+E. Thus E=-A Delta B-Delta A B+Delta A Delta B+Lambda^(-1)Delta C M^(-1) minus the omitted-product sum. [PDF p. 10 (B794), equations (4.21)-(4.25)]

For indices 0<=i,j

=p, the omitted-product contribution satisfies ||sum u^(i+j)Lambda^(-1)A^(i)B^(j)M^(-1)||_infinity lesssim (p-1)u^p||A||_infinity||B||_infinity. [PDF p. 10 (B794), equation (4.26)]

The accumulation-error estimate is ||Delta C||_infinity lesssim ((n+p^2)U+4rn theta^(-2)G_min)||A||_infinity||B||_infinity, where r is the maximum possible number of accumulation underflows in one output coefficient and r<=np(p+1)/2. The order-(n+p^2)U part is taken from Fasi et al.; the underflow extension is asserted by proceeding as in the single-word analysis. [PDF p. 11 (B795), equation (4.27) and preceding/following prose]

Combining the decomposition, omitted-product, and accumulation estimates gives ||E||_infinity lesssim (2zeta+zeta^2+(p-1)u^p+(n+p^2)U+2p(p+1)n^2 theta^(-2)G_min)||A||_infinity||B||_infinity. [PDF p. 11 (B795), equation (4.28)]

The cited range-unrestricted comparator is ||C_hat-AB||_infinity lesssim ((p+1)u^p+(n+p^2)U)||A||_infinity||B||_infinity; therefore (4.32) adds exactly the displayed input-underflow and accumulation-underflow terms. [PDF p. 11 (B795), equations (4.32)-(4.33); PDF p. 12 (B796), first comparison paragraph]

At the order level, the paper says multiword arithmetic reduces both input-format rounding and input-underflow errors by a factor of order u^(p-1), while sufficiently large p with u^p lesssim U+theta^(-2)G_min makes accumulation-format errors dominant. These are qualitative order comparisons, not additional exact inequalities. [PDF p. 12 (B796), post-(4.33) comparison]
definitions_and_conventions: The input format has u=2^(-t), f_min=2^(e_min), and f_max=2^(e_max)(2-2u); the accumulation format has U=2^(-T), F_min=2^(E_min), and F_max=2^(E_max)(2-2U), with T>=t and [E_min,E_max] containing [e_min,e_max]. [PDF p. 2 (B786), Model 1]

For round-to-nearest, g_min=f_min/2 without subnormals and g_min=u f_min with gradual underflow; analogously G_min=F_min/2 without subnormals and G_min=U F_min with gradual underflow. [PDF p. 2 (B786), equations (2.1)-(2.2)]

The relative-rounding and absolute-underflow errors are mutually exclusive on each operation: eta*delta=0 in both (2.3) and (2.4). [PDF p. 2 (B786), equation (2.3); PDF p. 3 (B787), equation (2.4) and following explanation]

The scaled p-word convention reconstructs a quantity using weighted words sum_{i=0}^{p-1}u^i w^(i), unlike the ordinary unweighted multiword recurrence; the weights are also used in the retained matrix products. [PDF p. 8 (B792), equations (4.1)-(4.3); PDF p. 11 (B795), equation (4.31)]

Delta A and Delta B use the sign convention exact matrix equals reconstructed matrix plus Delta; Delta C denotes aggregate errors arising while computing the retained word-product matrix products in the accumulation format; E=C_hat-AB is the total forward error. [PDF p. 10 (B794), equations (4.18)-(4.25)]

The symbol lesssim is used for simplified order bounds after higher-order terms are discarded; the paper explicitly introduces this convention when passing from (3.25) to (3.26), although it does not define a hidden constant formally. [PDF p. 7 (B791), paragraph before equation (3.26)]
implicit_context: The ranges i,j=0,...,p-1 and the interpretation of p as a positive number of words are supplied by the section 4 definition and are not separately quantified in Theorem 4.1. [PDF p. 8 (B792), section 4 and equations (4.1)-(4.3); PDF p. 11 (B795), equations (4.29)-(4.31)]

The proof uses the maximal power-of-two lower bounds from (3.4), notably lambda^(-1)<=2theta^(-1)||x||_infinity and its mu analogue, even though Theorem 4.1 restates only the upper bound on entries of Lambda A and BM. [PDF p. 5 (B789), equations (3.4a)-(3.4b); PDF p. 10 (B794), equations (4.15)-(4.16)]

Exact high-precision storage and exact outer power-of-two scaling are inherited from the setup surrounding (3.1), rather than restated in Theorem 4.1. [PDF p. 4 (B788), equation (3.1) and scaling-assumption paragraph; PDF p. 11 (B795), Theorem 4.1]

The order-(n+p^2)U component of (4.27) is a reused result from Fasi et al. [7, Thm. 2.1], not re-proved in the displayed derivation; the paper's own extension adds accumulation underflows by analogy with the preceding single-word analysis. [PDF p. 11 (B795), prose preceding equation (4.27)]
statement.algorithm_linkage: The selected result concerns the scaled p-word matrix-multiplication algorithm: choose row and column power-of-two scalings around theta, decompose Lambda A and BM with the weighted residual recurrences (4.29)-(4.30), form only the p(p+1)/2 products A^(i)B^(j) with i+j<p, weight each by u^(i+j), compute every constituent length-n inner product in the accumulation format, sum them, and apply Lambda^(-1) and M^(-1). Theorem 4.1 bounds the resulting C_hat, not an arbitrary multiword multiplication method. [PDF p. 5 (B789), equations (3.2)-(3.4); PDF p. 8 (B792), section 4 introduction; PDF p. 11 (B795), equations (4.29)-(4.32)]
numerical_model: Input conversion obeys fl(x)=x(1+delta)+eta with |delta|<=u, |eta|<=g_min, eta*delta=0, assuming no overflow. [PDF p. 2 (B786), equation (2.3)]
Each accumulation-format operation obeys FL(x op y)=(x op y)(1+delta)+eta with |delta|<=U, |eta|<=G_min, eta*delta=0, and op in {+,-,multiplication,division}. [PDF p. 3 (B787), equation (2.4)]

Round-to-nearest is the default model for all printed coefficients. Directed modes require doubling each format's relative and underflow parameters before applying the analysis. [PDF p. 3 (B787), paragraph following equation (2.4)]
Underflow is permitted and modeled as an absolute error, with separate constants for no-subnormal and gradual-underflow formats; overflow is excluded. [PDF p. 2 (B786), equations (2.1)-(2.3)]

Theorem 4.1 specifies accumulation-format inner products but does not separately spell out a summation order or fused-versus-unfused implementation. [PDF p. 11 (B795), sentence following equation (4.31); PDF p. 3 (B787), equation (2.4)]
error_notions: The main result is an absolute normwise forward-error bound for C_hat-AB, scaled on the right by ||A||_infinity||B||_infinity. [PDF p. 11 (B795), equation (4.32)]

Input-word rounding and underflow are represented by the decomposition residuals Delta A and Delta B; accumulation rounding and underflow are represented by Delta C; omitted pairs i+j>=p constitute a separate truncation contribution. [PDF p. 10 (B794), equations (4.18)-(4.26)]

The four displayed first-order contributions in (4.32) are, respectively, input-format rounding plus word-product omission, input-format underflow, accumulation-format rounding, and accumulation-format underflow. [PDF p. 10 (B794), equations (4.20) and (4.26); PDF p. 11 (B795), equations (4.27)-(4.32); PDF p. 12 (B796), first comparison paragraph]

Because underflow introduces products of row and column infinity norms rather than the componentwise quantity |x|^T|y|, the paper characterizes the available result as normwise rather than componentwise. [PDF p. 8 (B792), paragraph preceding section 4]
norms: The conclusion uses the matrix infinity norm on C_hat-AB, A, and B. [PDF p. 11 (B795), equations (4.32)-(4.33)]
The scaling construction uses vector infinity norms for each row x and column y. [PDF p. 5 (B789), equations (3.4a)-(3.4b)]
The max in the component residual estimate is componentwise before passage to the matrix infinity-norm bounds. [PDF p. 9 (B793), equation (4.13); PDF p. 10 (B794), sentence preceding equation (4.14)]
constants_and_indexing: theta=min(f_max,sqrt(F_max/n)), where n is the inner dimension and also the length of every matrix-product inner product. [PDF p. 5 (B789), equation (3.2); PDF p. 11 (B795), Theorem 4.1]
Word indices satisfy 0<=i,j=p within the p-by-p index square. [PDF p. 10 (B794), equations (4.21)-(4.26); PDF p. 11 (B795), equations (4.29)-(4.31)]

There are p(p+1)/2 retained word-product pairs. The maximum underflow count used in (4.27) is r<=n p(p+1)/2. [PDF p. 8 (B792), section 4 introduction; PDF p. 11 (B795), paragraph following equation (4.27)]

The four coefficients in (4.32) are exactly (p+1) on u^p, 4n on u^(p-1)theta^(-1)g_min, n+p^2 on U, and 2p(p+1)n^2 on theta^(-2)G_min, all inside one parenthesis multiplying ||A||_infinity||B||_infinity. [PDF p. 11 (B795), equation (4.32)]

The coefficient (p+1)u^p comes from 2zeta's rounding contribution plus the omitted-product term (p-1)u^p after higher-order simplification; the factor 2p(p+1)n^2 in the accumulation-underflow term results from substituting r<=np(p+1)/2 into 4rn. [PDF p. 10 (B794), equations (4.20) and (4.26); PDF p. 11 (B795), equations (4.27)-(4.32)]
higher_order_terms: Equation (4.28) retains the explicit zeta^2 contribution, whereas the simplified theorem bound (4.32) omits it. [PDF p. 11 (B795), equations (4.28) and (4.32)]

Equation (4.26) already uses lesssim when reducing the weighted omitted-product sum to (p-1)u^p, so factors and powers beyond the leading order are not asserted with an exact constant-one inequality. [PDF p. 10 (B794), construction inequality before and equation (4.26)]

The paper's explicit convention is that a lesssim bound is obtained by dropping second-order terms, as stated before (3.26); it gives no formal global definition of which mixed products or hidden constants lesssim permits. [PDF p. 7 (B791), paragraph before equation (3.26)]

The post-(4.33) statements about terms of order u^p, U, u^(p-1)theta^(-1)g_min, and theta^(-2)G_min suppress the displayed n- and p-dependent coefficients and are asymptotic comparisons rather than additional coefficient-sharp bounds. [PDF p. 12 (B796), post-(4.33) comparison]
exceptional_values: Overflow is excluded by the arithmetic models, and theta is chosen to prevent it in input conversion and accumulation. [PDF p. 2 (B786), equation (2.3); PDF p. 5 (B789), paragraph preceding equation (3.2)]
Underflow is explicitly allowed, either without subnormals or with gradual underflow, and is bounded by g_min or G_min. [PDF p. 2 (B786), equations (2.1)-(2.3)]

The outer storage/scaling context assumes no underflow or overflow before Lambda,M scaling or after Lambda^(-1),M^(-1) scaling. [PDF p. 4 (B788), equation (3.1) and following paragraph; PDF p. 5 (B789), continuation]

The selected theorem and Model 1 do not provide NaN or infinity propagation semantics; their equations operate on real quantities under the no-overflow assumption. [PDF p. 2 (B786), Model 1 and equation (2.3); PDF p. 3 (B787), equation (2.4)]

undebatable_constraints: The theorem is for A in R^(m by n) and B in R^(n by q), using the specific scaled p-word algorithm and Model 1. [PDF p. 11 (B795), Theorem 4.1]
The explicit theorem scaling condition uses theta=min(f_max,sqrt(F_max/n)) and power-of-two diagonal factors. [PDF p. 11 (B795), Theorem 4.1]
The proof's inverse-scaling estimates rely on the maximal power-of-two intervals (3.4a)-(3.4b). [PDF p. 5 (B789), equations (3.4a)-(3.4b); PDF p. 10 (B794), equations (4.15)-(4.16)]
The word recurrences include both division by u^i or u^j and weighted subtraction of all earlier words. [PDF p. 11 (B795), equations (4.29)-(4.30)]

Only pairs i+j

=p are an explicit omitted-product error. [PDF p. 10 (B794), equations (4.21)-(4.26); PDF p. 11 (B795), equation (4.31)]
All inner products forming A^(i)B^(j) are computed in the accumulation format. [PDF p. 11 (B795), sentence following equation (4.31)]
The conclusion is the four-term infinity-norm bound printed in (4.32), and every term multiplies ||A||_infinity||B||_infinity. [PDF p. 11 (B795), equation (4.32)]
Equation (4.33) removes only the two range-related underflow terms and retains (p+1)u^p and (n+p^2)U. [PDF p. 11 (B795), equations (4.32)-(4.33)]

The symbol in (4.32) is lesssim, not an exact <= relation; the paper associates lesssim with dropping higher-order terms. [PDF p. 7 (B791), paragraph before equation (3.26); PDF p. 11 (B795), equation (4.32)]
The printed coefficients assume round-to-nearest; directed rounding requires the parameter doublings stated after (2.4). [PDF p. 3 (B787), rounding-mode paragraph]
Underflow is included but overflow is assumed absent. [PDF p. 2 (B786), equations (2.1)-(2.3)]

The post-(4.33) factor-u^(p-1) claim is an order statement, and its citation of a 4n single-word input-underflow term conflicts with the 4n^2 term printed in (3.26). [PDF p. 7 (B791), equation (3.26); PDF p. 12 (B796), post-(4.33) comparison]

ambiguities.issue: Theorem 4.1 explicitly requires only that entries of Lambda A and BM be bounded above by theta, but the derivation also needs the scalings to be maximal powers of two. [PDF p. 11 (B795), Theorem 4.1; PDF p. 5 (B789), equations (3.4a)-(3.4b)]
ambiguities.evidence: The bounds lambda^(-1)<=2theta^(-1)||x||_infinity and mu^(-1)<=2theta^(-1)||y||_infinity follow from the omitted lower bounds theta/(2||x||_infinity)<lambda and theta/(2||y||_infinity)<mu, and equation (4.16) uses the lambda bound. [PDF p. 5 (B789), equations (3.4a)-(3.4b); PDF p. 10 (B794), equations (4.15)-(4.16)]
ambiguities.impact: Read literally with arbitrary smaller power-of-two scalings, the theorem's explicit hypotheses do not control inverse-scaled underflow by the displayed constants; the maximal-scaling condition must be treated as inherited intent or as a missing hypothesis. [PDF p. 10 (B794), equations (4.15)-(4.20); PDF p. 11 (B795), equation (4.32)]

ambiguities.issue: The single-word comparison after (4.33) says equation (3.26) has input-underflow term 4n theta^(-1)g_min, while (3.26) actually prints 4n^2 theta^(-1)g_min. [PDF p. 7 (B791), equation (3.26); PDF p. 12 (B796), post-(4.33) comparison]
ambiguities.evidence: Equation (4.32) has 4n u^(p-1)theta^(-1)g_min. The prose claims this is obtained from 4n theta^(-1)g_min by an order-u^(p-1) reduction, but the displayed single-word normwise bound has an additional factor n. [PDF p. 11 (B795), equation (4.32); PDF p. 12 (B796), comparison with (3.26)]
ambiguities.impact: The source does not resolve whether the prose misquotes (3.26), whether (4.32) is intentionally sharper at p=1, or whether one displayed coefficient is erroneous; the claimed reduction factor is therefore only unambiguous at the level of u dependence with n treated as fixed. [PDF p. 7 (B791), equations (3.25)-(3.26); PDF p. 12 (B796), post-(4.33) comparison]

ambiguities.issue: Equation (4.31) writes C, not C_hat, on the left while introducing an approximation that retains only i+j<p; the next sentence distinguishes the computed C_hat. [PDF p. 11 (B795), equation (4.31) and following sentence]
ambiguities.evidence: The preceding derivation more precisely writes C_hat=Lambda^(-1)(sum_{i+j<p}u^(i+j)A^(i)B^(j)+Delta C)M^(-1) and then C_hat=AB+E. [PDF p. 10 (B794), equations (4.21)-(4.25)]
ambiguities.impact: Equation (4.31) should be read as the algorithmic prescription or ideal retained-word sum, not as an exact identity equating AB with a generally truncated decomposition. [PDF p. 10 (B794), equations (4.21)-(4.26); PDF p. 11 (B795), equations (4.31)-(4.32)]

ambiguities.issue: The paper does not formally define lesssim or its hidden constant; it only explains one use as dropping second-order terms. [PDF p. 7 (B791), paragraph before equation (3.26)]
ambiguities.evidence: Equations (4.26)-(4.28), (4.32), and (4.33) all use lesssim, while (4.28) still displays zeta^2 and (4.32) drops it. [PDF p. 10 (B794), equation (4.26); PDF p. 11 (B795), equations (4.27)-(4.33)]
ambiguities.impact: The coefficients in (4.32) are leading-order displayed coefficients and cannot be interpreted as a literal exact inequality with constant one or with a fully specified remainder. [PDF p. 11 (B795), equations (4.28) and (4.32)]

ambiguities.issue: The recurrences (4.29)-(4.30) place one input-format fl around a residual expression but do not specify the arithmetic precision used internally to form the sum, subtraction, and division. [PDF p. 11 (B795), equations (4.29)-(4.30)]
ambiguities.evidence: The analysis treats the residual expression mathematically and then rounds it with fl, whereas only the later inner products are explicitly assigned to the accumulation format. [PDF p. 9 (B793), equations (4.8)-(4.13); PDF p. 11 (B795), sentence following equation (4.31)]
ambiguities.impact: A concrete implementation that rounds intermediate recurrence operations separately is not explicitly covered unless it realizes the same effective fl of the exact residual. [PDF p. 11 (B795), equations (4.29)-(4.30)]

ambiguities.issue: Theorem 4.1 specifies that inner products use the accumulation format but does not state a summation order or whether multiplication and addition are fused. [PDF p. 11 (B795), sentence following equation (4.31)]
ambiguities.evidence: Model 1 supplies a per-operation FL model for +, -, multiplication, and division, and (4.27) imports the order-(n+p^2)U estimate from Fasi et al. rather than restating an operation sequence. [PDF p. 3 (B787), equation (2.4); PDF p. 11 (B795), prose preceding equation (4.27)]
ambiguities.impact: The source contract fixes the format and retained word products but leaves lower-level MMA evaluation order inherited from the cited analysis or hardware model. [PDF p. 11 (B795), equations (4.27)-(4.31)]

contract_plain_english: For real A of size m-by-n and B of size n-by-q, use maximal row and column power-of-two scalings intended to place the scaled entries near theta=min(f_max,sqrt(F_max/n)), form p weighted input-format words by the residual recurrences (4.29)-(4.30), retain exactly the pairs i+j<p, compute every resulting inner product in the accumulation format, and undo the scaling. [PDF p. 5 (B789), equations (3.2)-(3.4); PDF p. 11 (B795), Theorem 4.1 and equations (4.29)-(4.31)] Under Model 1's round-to-nearest, underflow-aware, no-overflow assumptions, the computed C_hat has the leading-order infinity-norm forward bound ((p+1)u^p+4n u^(p-1)theta^(-1)g_min+(n+p^2)U+2p(p+1)n^2 theta^(-2)G_min)||A||_infinity||B||_infinity. [PDF p. 2 (B786), Model 1; PDF p. 3 (B787), rounding-mode paragraph; PDF p. 11 (B795), equation (4.32)] The first and third terms are the range-unrestricted terms in (4.33); the second and fourth account for input and accumulation underflow. The bound is a lesssim, higher-order-suppressed statement, not an exact constant-one inequality. [PDF p. 7 (B791), paragraph before equation (3.26); PDF p. 11 (B795), equations (4.32)-(4.33)] The paper's qualitative claim that multiword arithmetic reduces input rounding and input underflow equally by order u^(p-1) is subject to the unresolved 4n versus 4n^2 discrepancy in its comparison with the single-word bound. [PDF p. 7 (B791), equation (3.26); PDF p. 12 (B796), post-(4.33) comparison]
